ai-hpc.h3: OpenAI cuts off Cursor after SpaceX buys the coding editor
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI will end direct model access inside Cursor on 12 November, weeks after SpaceX closed its acquisition of maker Anysphere.
body: OpenAI said on 28 August it is winding down the contract that supplies its models to the coding editor Cursor, with direct access ending on 12 November 2026. The company said that is the maximum notice its change of control clause allows after SpaceX completed its purchase of Cursor developer Anysphere in mid August.

OpenAI framed the decision around trust rather than product overlap, saying it cannot be confident SpaceX will use the technology within OpenAI terms of service given its experience with Elon Musk companies. Cursor will not receive any newly released OpenAI models during the wind down period.

For Cursor users the practical effect is a forced migration to Anthropic models, xAI models or Cursor in house models before the November cutoff. The split is the sharpest sign yet that model supply is becoming a strategic weapon between rival AI camps.

ai-hpc.h3: Nvidia pauses cloud revenue sharing deals on antitrust worries
ai-hpc.summary: Nvidia has halted some of the backstop agreements it announced in July, reportedly over concern they could attract antitrust scrutiny.
body: Nvidia has paused parts of the cloud revenue sharing programme it launched in July, under which it acts as a financial backstop for operators building large GPU clusters in exchange for a cut of operating revenue. The arrangement also commits Nvidia to renting back unused GPUs at a fixed rate.

Reporting from the Wall Street Journal, relayed by Reuters, said the pause reflects concern the structure could invite antitrust attention. Nvidia told DCD the July model remains in place and continues to evolve because of high demand. Firmus and Sharon AI were among the first adopters, with Firmus deploying 170,000 GPUs in Batam, Indonesia.

The news landed days after Nvidia posted quarterly revenue of $96.2 billion, up 106 percent year on year, and disclosed $108.5 billion in guarantees and related agreements tied to enabling AI cloud computing.

ai-hpc.h3: Nvidia pushes its moat past the GPU with Vera Rubin racks
ai-hpc.summary: The Vera Rubin generation pairs the Rubin GPU with a Vera CPU, an inference accelerator and matched storage and networking racks.
body: Nvidia is rolling out Vera Rubin, an architecture that surrounds the Rubin GPU with purpose built companions including the Vera CPU, the Groq 3 LPX inference accelerator and dedicated storage and networking racks. The design treats everything outside the accelerator as part of the product rather than an afterthought.

The Vera CPU is aimed squarely at data orchestration. Nvidia argues there is a hard ceiling on how much memory fits in any single server, so moving data efficiently between tiers becomes the limiting factor on large inference jobs.

Analysts increasingly describe the company advantage as CUDA software, networking, system architecture and developer habit rather than raw silicon alone. Morgan Stanley has flagged the CPU and networking lines as growth contributors and pointed to Nvidia claims of lower cost per token than rivals.

ai-hpc.h3: Lambda raises $1B in private debt to buy more Nvidia chips
ai-hpc.summary: The neocloud will lease the GPUs to Microsoft, adding to a run of loans that underlines how debt funded the AI buildout has become.
body: Lambda has raised $1 billion in short dated private debt, arranged by JP Morgan Chase, to buy Nvidia accelerators that it will lease to Microsoft. The short tenor signals the company expects to deploy the hardware and start generating cash quickly enough to repay lenders.

It is the latest in a string of facilities. Lambda closed a $1 billion senior secured credit line in May and this week completed a $926 million term loan to fund Nvidia GB300 GPUs for a contracted deployment. The company is also reported to be in talks for a $3 billion pre IPO round after raising $1.5 billion last November at a $5.43 billion valuation.
Bloomberg data cited by TechCrunch puts total AI related debt raised by banks and tech companies globally above $400 billion so far in 2026.

ai-hpc.h3: SK hynix breaks ground on $4bn HBM packaging plant in Indiana
ai-hpc.summary: The West Lafayette site is the memory maker's first US high bandwidth memory packaging base, with mass production slated for 2029.
body: SK hynix held a groundbreaking ceremony on 27 August at Purdue University in West Lafayette for an advanced packaging plant costing more than $4 billion. The 133.5 acre site will be the company first high bandwidth memory packaging base in the United States.

The cleanroom is expected to open by October 2028, with mass production of next generation HBM starting in the second half of 2029. SK hynix says the plant will employ around 1,000 people at full capacity and support roughly 7,000 jobs once construction, operations and suppliers are counted.

Under the CHIPS and Science Act the US government committed up to $458 million in direct funding plus $500 million in loans. The company chief executive said Indiana will be a key memory production base by 2030.

ai-hpc.h3: New US chip tariffs could reach data center servers
ai-hpc.summary: The Trump administration is weighing further semiconductor tariffs that may extend to finished goods including servers, Politico reports.
body: The White House is considering an expansion of semiconductor tariffs that would cover not only chips but products built around them, with data center servers named as a candidate category. Tariffs are paid by importers, so the cost would land on operators buying kit for US sites.

Discussions remain early and a phase in period is under consideration. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick is said to favour using the threat to force investment in domestic chip manufacturing, with companies that commit capital escaping the levy. A White House spokesperson said reshoring semiconductor manufacturing is a top priority.

The Computer and Communications Industry Association warned in June that tariffs could cost about $90 billion in annual US GDP and delay or cancel roughly 20 percent of data center projects planned through 2030.

ai-hpc.h3: Trump emergency order targets foreign made grid equipment
ai-hpc.summary: A 26 August executive order restricts foreign bulk power equipment and lets DOE impose conditions on gear already in service.
body: President Trump declared a national emergency over the US bulk power system, directing the Energy Department to restrict certain foreign produced grid equipment and to set conditions on equipment already installed. The order covers transformers, generators, inverters, batteries, turbines and control systems, plus associated software, firmware and remote access capability.

For AI campuses the timing is awkward. Transformers and switchgear already face long lead times, and DOE has 120 days to publish rules defining covered equipment and suppliers. Jefferies analysts expect the restrictions to lengthen lead times further and lift domestic prices.

Analyst Neil Osnato of Persistence Analytics Group said the practical shift is that equipment origin, vendor control, software and lifecycle dependencies now become part of a reliability determination rather than a pure procurement decision. NERC said it will work with DOE and FERC on implementation.

ai-hpc.h3: Italian grid queue for data centers passes 95GW
ai-hpc.summary: Connection requests filed with Terna have climbed from 1GW in 2021 to 95.38GW, with Lombardy alone accounting for 49GW.
body: Data center operators have now lodged 95.38GW of grid connection requests with Italian transmission operator Terna, up from 31.28GW in 2024 and about 1GW in 2021. Of 531 requests filed since 2021, some 300 arrived in the past eight months.
Lombardy dominates with 290 requests totalling 49GW, most of them clustered around Milan. Lazio, Piedmont and Apulia account for most of the remainder.

Terna is developing 27 electrical substations to absorb the demand, five of which already have local authorisation. As elsewhere in Europe, the queue figure vastly exceeds what will actually be built, but it shows how quickly speculative AI capacity is being parked in grid pipelines.

ai-hpc.h3: Data center backlash starts costing incumbents their seats
ai-hpc.summary: At least 18 sitting officeholders lost elections in a year after documented action on a data center project or policy fight.
body: A Data Center Knowledge review of election results, government records and local reporting counted at least 18 incumbent officeholders who lost between August 2025 and August 2026 after a documented vote, approval, incentive or public advocacy tied to a data center. The review does not claim the issue decided every race.

Utah produced the clearest cases. State Senate President J. Stuart Adams lost a June Republican primary after being linked to the proposed Stratos project in Box Elder County, and two county commissioners who voted to advance it also lost. In Festus, Missouri, four council members lost after a fight over a proposed $6 billion project, including one who had voted against it.

Industry figures concede the sector was not built to campaign locally. Tigercomm president Mike Casey said too many developers try to bulldoze projects through instead of campaigning for them, turning a community relations problem into a political crisis.

ai-hpc.h3: Anthropic paper shows AI fixing its own alignment failures
ai-hpc.summary: Automated researchers improved scores on all 10 misalignment benchmarks they were given, without degrading general performance.
body: Anthropic published a paper on 28 August titled Automated Researchers Can Reliably Mitigate Alignment Failures, led by fellow Chen Yueh-Han. Given 10 benchmarks for specific misaligned behaviours, the automated systems improved performance on every one of them while leaving overall capability intact.

The system mimics the human research loop. Each agent searches the literature, proposes a method, trains for 30 minutes and iterates, keeping what works and discarding what does not. The paper reports that the best automated method beats what experienced humans propose on average within six hours, and puts the cost at roughly $4 per hour of API inference against $150 per hour for a human researcher.

The authors flag limits. The approach only works insofar as the benchmarks capture the real alignment target, and someone still has to build and maintain those benchmarks and the literature the agents draw on.

ai-hpc.h3: Meta framework lifts an 8B model to Claude Opus 4.5 level
ai-hpc.summary: EvoHarness-RL teaches a small model when to read, update or consolidate context, closing a 49 point gap on ALFWorld.
body: Researchers at Meta AI and the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign introduced EvoHarness-RL, a framework that adds a layer of abstraction to an agent harness and trains the underlying model on when to read, update or consolidate information from its environment.

On the ALFWorld benchmark, a text environment built around multi step tasks and state tracking, a Qwen3-8B model reached a 96.9 percent average success rate with the framework. That is 49.0 percentage points above its ReAct baseline and marginally above the 96.4 percent Claude Opus 4.5 scores out of the box.

The result feeds a broader argument that harness engineering, not parameter count, is where a lot of remaining agent performance sits. For buyers it points at running cheaper open models for well scoped workflows instead of routing everything to a frontier endpoint.

ai-hpc.h3: Open weight labs become Silicon Valley's hottest targets
ai-hpc.summary: Nvidia is closing on Hugging Face at about $12.9bn, following Stripe buying OpenRouter and Nvidia's $6bn Poolside deal.
body: Nvidia has agreed to buy Hugging Face, the model and dataset hub with more than 13 million registered users, for about $12.9 billion according to reporting from The Information. Business Insider had earlier described the two as in talks without a signed deal.

The purchase sits inside a pattern. Nvidia struck a $6 billion agreement with open weight model builder Poolside, with most staff moving across, and Stripe bought OpenRouter, the largest supplier of open weight models to businesses, for more than $7 billion.

The common thread is that huge sums are flowing into a corner of the market built on giving weights away. Buyers appear to be paying for distribution and developer gravity rather than for model IP itself.

ai-hpc.h3: Huang declares AGI again as the term keeps sliding
ai-hpc.summary: The Nvidia chief repeated his claim that the company has reached artificial general intelligence, on a definition few others share.
body: Jensen Huang told an audience that Nvidia has achieved artificial general intelligence, a claim he has now made more than once. The Verge notes that the assertion rests on a definition loose enough to make it close to unfalsifiable.

The point is less about capability than about vocabulary. AGI has drifted from a research milestone to a marketing register, and the industry has no shared test that would settle whether anyone has crossed it.

The timing is convenient. Nvidia is arguing that its full stack of accelerators, CPUs, networking and software is the platform on which any such system would run, which makes a maximalist framing of progress commercially useful.

ai-hpc.h3: Tencent open sources Hy4 preview with 770B parameters
ai-hpc.summary: Hunyuan's next generation model activates 49B parameters and handles a context window above one million tokens.
body: Tencent Hunyuan released and open sourced Hy4 preview on 28 August. The model carries 770 billion total parameters with 49 billion activated and a context window exceeding one million tokens. It ships through WorkBuddy, CodeBuddy, Yuanbao and ima, with API access via Tencent Cloud TokenHub and OpenRouter.

Pricing is set at $0.834 per million input tokens and $2.501 per million output tokens, with two weeks of free access in WorkBuddy and CodeBuddy. Tencent aims the model at coding, office work, data analysis, game development and scientific research.

In an internal blind evaluation using 163 experts and 203 engineering tasks, Hy4 preview averaged 2.99 out of 4 against 2.92 for GLM 5.3 and 2.94 for Kimi K3. Tencent also said the model helped tune its own training and inference stack, lifting end to end throughput 31.8 percent over baseline.

ai-hpc.h3: Zhipu confirms Ox Alpha was GLM-5.3-Flash and ships weights
ai-hpc.summary: The 320B parameter model with 18B active is the first natively multimodal entry in the GLM-5 series.
body: Zhipu released GLM-5.3-Flash along with its weights, confirming that the model tested anonymously as Ox Alpha belongs to the GLM family. It has 320 billion total parameters and 18 billion active.
The release is the first natively multimodal model in the GLM-5 series, taking text, images, video, visual documents and interleaved multimodal inputs. Weights are published on Hugging Face.
Zhipu ran the model anonymously on OpenRouter and OpenCode before announcing it, a now common tactic that lets Chinese labs collect neutral community benchmarks before the brand is attached.

ai-hpc.h3: China's daily AI token calls pass 500 trillion
ai-hpc.summary: Aggregate model processing hit the mark by June 2026 as agent workflows multiplied inference demand.
body: Daily AI token call volume across China exceeded 500 trillion as of June 2026, a measure of aggregate model processing rather than user or model counts. Industry representatives said model update cycles have compressed from roughly three months to four to six weeks.

Agent workflows are a large part of the jump. They repeatedly retrieve information, read context, call tools and process feedback, so a single task can consume orders of magnitude more inference than a chat turn.

Tencent offered one datapoint on the slope, saying Hunyuan 3 recorded 68 times more token calls than Hunyuan 2 in its first week. The figures help explain why Chinese cloud providers are racing to compress data center delivery timelines.

ai-hpc.h3: MiniMax enterprise and open platform revenue jumps 703%
ai-hpc.summary: First half revenue from the open platform and enterprise services reached $73.9m, overtaking the company's consumer AI products.
body: MiniMax reported first half 2026 results showing open platform and enterprise AI service revenue up 703.1 percent year on year to $73.9 million. That line now accounts for 63.4 percent of total revenue, against 30.3 percent a year earlier.

Revenue from AI native products rose 100.9 percent to $42.6 million, while gross profit climbed 464.8 percent to $20.8 million. The platform business has therefore overtaken consumer facing products as the larger contributor.
The mix shift matches a wider pattern among Chinese model developers, where selling API access and enterprise deployment has proved easier to scale than consumer subscription revenue.

ai-hpc.h3: PsiBot raises over $100m as industrial backers pile in
ai-hpc.summary: The dexterous manipulation startup drew money from Tuopu Group, a Chery backed fund, Lens Technology and Fosun Fortune Capital.
body: Chinese embodied AI company PsiBot has closed a funding round of more than $100 million. Investors include Ningbo Tuopu Group, a Chery Holdings backed fund, Lens Technology, 37 Interactive Entertainment, Wuhu Investment Holding Group and Fosun Fortune Capital, with existing shareholder Zhuhai Technology Industry Group following on.
The capital is earmarked for embodied world model research, human operation data collection and deployments in logistics and advanced manufacturing.

PsiBot is building a dual system architecture that pairs its Psi-R2 operation policy model with the Psi-W0 action conditioned world model. The investor list is notable for how heavily it skews toward industrial and automotive supply chain names rather than pure venture funds.

ai-hpc.h3: Baidu launches DuMateBench to score what agents deliver
ai-hpc.summary: The leaderboard covers more than 200 office tasks across six categories and grades completed output rather than answers.
body: Baidu has launched DuMateBench, an evaluation leaderboard built to measure whether AI agents actually finish real work and hand back usable output. It contains more than 200 office tasks spread across six categories and tests performance in complex operating environments.

The benchmark scores task understanding, tool use, continuous execution and final result delivery. It uses a general evaluation framework with open interfaces so different models and agent stacks can be compared under identical criteria.
The framing is the point. Baidu is trying to shift assessment from what a model can answer to what an agent can complete and deliver, which is closer to how enterprise buyers judge deployments.

ai-hpc.h3: Salesforce puts its CRM inside Claude under Claudeforce deal
ai-hpc.summary: A plugin with 37 prebuilt sales skills lets sellers query and act on live CRM data without opening Salesforce at all.
body: Salesforce and Anthropic announced Claudeforce, an expanded partnership that makes Claude the reasoning engine across the Salesforce ecosystem and exposes Salesforce data, workflows, business logic and governance to agentic use.

The centrepiece is Salesforce in Claude, a plugin shipping with 37 prebuilt sales skills covering meeting preparation, deal health reviews and pipeline analysis. Sellers can query, update and act on live CRM records from inside Claude. It is with selected pilot customers now, with open beta planned for September and skills for other business functions following.

Anthropic is also embedding Claude into the Agentforce Atlas Reasoning Engine. The arrangement cuts against the model agnostic posture most enterprise software vendors have publicly held, tying a core system of record to one lab.

ai-hpc.h3: Caterpillar ports mining autonomy lessons into AI rollout
ai-hpc.summary: The industrial group is applying decades of automated haul truck experience to deploying AI across jobsites and its own workforce.
body: Caterpillar built its autonomy business in mining, where labour shortages and hazardous conditions made automation worth the cost. Chief technology officer Jaime Mineart says the company is now carrying that experience into more dynamic settings such as construction sites and quarries.

Its Cat AI Assistant lets field technicians standing beside a machine use voice commands to pull repair procedures, troubleshoot faults and identify parts before starting work. The tool draws on roughly 1.6 million connected assets and more than 16 petabytes of structured data. Caterpillar also uses agents internally to modernise legacy code, generate and test software and catch defects earlier.

Mineart argues the hard part is not the technology but rewiring workflows and roles around it. The company plans to spend $100 million over five years training its 118,000 employees, while its power generation division saw sales rise 72 percent to $3.10 billion on data center demand.

ai-hpc.h3: ChatGPT Work can now sign in to sites and act alone
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI's work agent can book appointments, cancel reservations and complete applications without OpenAI seeing the credentials.
body: OpenAI has given ChatGPT Work the ability to sign in to third party websites and carry out tasks end to end, including booking a DMV appointment, cancelling a reservation or filling in a job application. The company says it never sees the login credentials used.
The change moves the product past retrieval and drafting into taking actions with real world consequences on a user account. Sam Altman flagged the update publicly as a significant step.

It also raises the stakes on error handling and authorisation. An agent that can authenticate as the user is one that can submit forms, spend money and trigger irreversible actions if its judgement or its instructions go wrong.

ai-hpc.h3: Judge voids Pentagon's supply chain risk label on Anthropic
ai-hpc.summary: US District Judge Rita Lin called the designation unlawful retaliation and ordered it removed, handing Anthropic its first court win.
body: A federal judge ruled that the Defense Department decision to designate Anthropic a supply chain risk was unlawful and ordered the label removed. Judge Rita Lin found the move by Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth amounted to unlawful retaliation in violation of the First Amendment and was arbitrary and capricious, and said Anthropic was denied due process.

The dispute began earlier this year when Anthropic refused to strip internal safety guardrails that block military use of Claude in autonomous weapons and mass surveillance. Lin noted that other parts of the government kept working with the company after the designation, writing that none of that squares with a genuine fear of sabotage.
A second Anthropic suit over the same label remains before a court in Washington DC, so the fight is not finished.

ai-hpc.h3: Sony and Warner publishers sue Anthropic over song training
ai-hpc.summary: The suit filed late Friday names Dario Amodei and Benjamin Mann and seeks up to $150,000 per infringed composition.
body: Sony Music Publishing and Warner Chappell Music sued Anthropic in federal court in northern California, naming the company alongside chief executive Dario Amodei and co-founder Benjamin Mann. The publishers describe the conduct as one of the largest and most blatant ongoing thefts of intellectual property in history.

The complaint alleges Anthropic illegally torrented, scraped and downloaded tens of thousands of copyrighted compositions to train Claude, a far broader set of works than earlier suits targeted. Cited songs include Eye of the Tiger and Taylor Swift's Paper Rings. The publishers want a jury trial and statutory damages of up to $150,000 per composition.

A 2023 case brought by Universal Music Group, Concord and ABKCO already produced court approved guardrails requiring Anthropic to block reproduction of copyrighted lyrics in outputs. With this filing all three major music publishers are now litigating against the company at once.

ai-hpc.h3: New Jersey makes data centers report energy and water use
ai-hpc.summary: Governor Mikie Sherrill signed S3379, requiring semiannual disclosures from facilities above 100MW to the Board of Public Utilities.
body: New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill signed S3379 on 27 August, requiring data centers to file reports every six months with the state Board of Public Utilities. The rules apply to existing and new facilities with capacity above 100MW.

Operators must disclose total energy consumption, the split between cooling and IT load, peak daily water use, water sources and both on site and backup power supplies. Critics say self reporting falls short of what residents calling for a statewide pause had asked for.

The law follows July legislation that required data center firms to bring their own clean energy and created a separate utility rate class for large loads to stop costs shifting onto ordinary ratepayers.

ai-hpc.h3: Abbott halts Texas state funding for Flock AI cameras
ai-hpc.summary: The order came as a state agency was found to have put at least $30m into building out the surveillance network.
body: Texas Governor Greg Abbott ordered all state agencies to pause funding for Flock cameras, the AI powered automated licence plate readers that have spread across US policing. His spokesman confirmed the Thursday night directive on Friday.

The order landed as the Texas Tribune prepared an investigation showing the Motor Vehicle Crime Prevention Authority, whose board is mostly appointed by Abbott, had devoted at least $30 million to grants for local departments. At least 3,200 Flock cameras have been installed since 2023, including almost 1,200 by the Department of Public Safety under a three year $15.9 million contract.

The pause only covers state dollars, so agencies can still buy the cameras with federal money. Opposition to warrantless AI tracking has become unusually bipartisan, and Abbott is the highest profile Republican yet to act on it.

ai-hpc.h3: Over 100 firms call for a global surge in AI cyber defense
ai-hpc.summary: OpenAI, Anthropic and Google signed an open letter arguing defenders need cyber capable AI before attackers scale up.
body: An open letter signed by more than 100 companies and organisations, including OpenAI, Anthropic and Google, calls for what it terms a global surge in cyber defence. The signatories argue AI enabled attacks will become far more widespread and sophisticated.

The core ask is to put cyber capable AI in the hands of defenders, starting with teams protecting essential services, then fix the most dangerous weaknesses, verify the fixes and publish what worked so others can copy it.

The letter follows a run of incidents in which AI systems were used or went rogue in real intrusions, including the OpenAI and Hugging Face episode. Critics will note that the labs proposing the remedy are also the suppliers of the capability that created the problem.

ai-hpc.h3: UK Green Party demands a nationwide data center moratorium
ai-hpc.summary: The party would permit only local scale facilities serving local communities, halting large builds across the country.
body: The UK Green Party has called for a nationwide moratorium on data center construction, saying only local scale data centers for the local community should be allowed to proceed.
The position goes further than most European objections, which have focused on grid connection queues, water use and planning conditions rather than an outright national stop.

It arrives while Britain is courting AI investment and preparing for a change of prime minister, putting the party at odds with the government pitch that data center capacity is a prerequisite for domestic AI capability.
